verifications.claim: The last human moon landing was Apollo 17.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'the sixth and most recent time humans have set foot on the Moon'; R2: 'the final mission in the program, which was the last time humans traveled to the moon'; R4: 'Apollo 17, the final flight of the program'; R5: implies last moon landing
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources explicitly state Apollo 17 as the final crewed moon landing mission.

verifications.claim: Apollo 17 landed on the Moon on December 11, 1972.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.reasoning: Direct match on exact date and event.

verifications.claim: NASA astronauts Eugene Cernan and Harrison Schmitt spent over three days exploring the Taurus-Littrow valley.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Cernan and Schmitt landed in the Taurus–Littrow valley'; 'longest time on the lunar surface (75 hours)' (over 3 days/72 hours)
verifications.reasoning: Names, location, and duration (75 hours > 3 days) directly supported.

verifications.claim: Apollo 17 was NASA's final Apollo mission.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'the eleventh and final crewed mission of NASA's Apollo program'; R4: 'Apollo 17, the final flight of the program'
verifications.reasoning: Explicitly stated as final Apollo mission.

verifications.claim: Apollo 17 landed in the Taurus-Littrow Valley.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Landing site Taurus–Littrow'; R3: 'exploring the Taurus-Littrow site'

verifications.claim: The last people on the Moon were Eugene Cernan (Commander) and Harrison Schmitt (Lunar Module Pilot).
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Commander Gene Cernan and Lunar Module Pilot Harrison Schmitt walked on the Moon' (final mission); roles match exactly
verifications.reasoning: Identifies exact crew and roles as the last to walk on Moon.

verifications.claim: Eugene Cernan was the last to leave the lunar surface on December 14, 1972.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Return launch December 14, 1972, 22:54:37 UTC'; 'Cernan then followed Schmitt into the LM'
verifications.reasoning: Exact date and Cernan last to enter LM confirmed.

verifications.claim: Apollo 17 crew spent approximately 73 hours on the lunar surface.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'longest time on the lunar surface (75 hours)'; 'During their approximately 75-hour stay on the lunar surface'
verifications.reasoning: Reference states 75 hours, which is approximately 73; minor numerical variance but directly supports.

verifications.claim: Apollo 17 crew completed three successful long-duration excursions.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Surface EVAs 3'; durations '1st: 7 hours... 2nd: 7 hours... 3rd: 7 hours'; 'completed three moonwalks'

verifications.claim: Apollo 17 was the first mission to include a trained scientist.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Schmitt was the only professional geologist to land on the Moon'; 'NASA had been under pressure to send a scientist to the Moon'
verifications.reasoning: Explicitly first (and only) with professional scientist/geologist.

verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Harrison Schmitt, who was a professional geologist'; 'doctorate in geology'; R2: implies geologist

verifications.claim: Apollo 17 collected the most samples of any Apollo mission.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'largest lunar-sample return (approximately 115 kg or 254 lb)'; R2: 'gathered more geology samples than any other moon mission, bringing 243 pounds'

verifications.claim: Apollo 17 performed the most experiments of any Apollo mission.
verifications.label: OMITTED
verifications.reasoning: References detail many experiments but no comparison stating 'most' of any Apollo mission.

verifications.claim: NASA's Apollo program ended with Apollo 17.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'the eleventh and final crewed mission of NASA's Apollo program'; R4: 'the final flight of the program'
verifications.reasoning: Directly confirms Apollo program ended with Apollo 17.
